facts.text: The team and skills needed are the distinct specialist disciplines a manufacturer must have in place simultaneously to build and defend a virtual validation capability.
facts.quote: The team and skills needed are the distinct specialist disciplines a manufacturer must have in place at the same time to build and defend a virtual validation capability.

facts.text: Chapter 2 derives virtual-validation staffing disciplines from European research-program partner lists and accepted workflow requirements; the result is expert synthesis, not a published staffing prescription.
facts.quote: Chapter 2 derives the disciplines from the partner lists of the European research programs and from what accepted workflows require, as expert synthesis rather than a published staffing prescription

facts.text: Chapter 2 identifies the needed disciplines as safety, requirements and scenario engineering; perception and sensor modeling; machine dynamics and braking; simulation and MIL, SIL and HIL engineering; test automation and data engineering; physical testing and ground truth; statistics and model credibility; functional safety, safety arguments and supplier integration.
facts.quote: simulation and model-, software- and hardware-in-the-loop engineering; test automation and data engineering; physical-test and ground-truth engineering; statistics and model credibility; functional-safety and safety-argument specialists plus supplier integration

facts.text: Chapter 2 calls for one credibility argument per sensor type in virtual validation.
facts.quote: perception and sensor-model specialists, one credibility argument per sensor type

facts.text: Chapter 2 calls for an independent safety or acceptance authority able to reject virtual-validation evidence.
facts.quote: an independent safety or acceptance authority able to reject the evidence [Chapter 2]

facts.text: Chapter 11 identifies tool-side skills covering simulation architecture and co-simulation; heavy-machine dynamics; tires, tracks, soil and braking; camera, radar, lidar and ultrasonic modeling; Unreal, OpenUSD and 3D assets; scenario and V&V automation; data engineering; cloud and continuous integration; ECU and HIL work; statistics and coverage; and functional safety.
facts.quote: Unreal, OpenUSD and 3D asset engineering; scenario and verification and validation (V&V) automation; data engineering; cloud and continuous integration; electronic control unit (ECU) and hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) work; statistics and coverage; functional safety.

facts.text: An open-source virtual-validation build needs simulation software engineers, rendering specialists, multibody and terramechanics experts, sensor physicists and test-automation engineers.
facts.quote: An open-source build needs simulation software engineers, rendering specialists, multibody and terramechanics experts, sensor physicists and test-automation engineers

facts.text: A bought virtual-validation stack needs tool specialists, scenario engineers and safety staff.
facts.quote: a bought stack needs tool specialists, scenario engineers and safety staff

facts.text: A partner model for virtual validation needs a smaller internal core that owns requirements and acceptance.
facts.quote: a partner model needs a smaller internal core that owns requirements and acceptance [Chapter 11]

facts.text: No team-size figure for the virtual-validation capability was found anywhere.
facts.quote: Team size was not found anywhere.

facts.text: For scale, the PEGASUS program addressing one highway function took 17 partners, 42 months and about 1,791 person-months.
facts.quote: For scale, the PEGASUS program on one highway function took 17 partners, 42 months and about 1,791 person-months [Chapter 2].

facts.text: Chapter 12 asks the virtual-validation plan to identify named owners, key-person cover, an independent assessor, a red team and skill gaps.
facts.quote: Chapter 12 asks the plan for named owners, key-person cover, an independent assessor, a red team and a list of skill gaps

facts.text: Chapter 13 insists that independence be designed into virtual validation: model developers should not be the only people deciding whether discrepancies are acceptable.
facts.quote: Chapter 13 insists that independence be designed in: model developers should not be the only people deciding whether discrepancies are acceptable.

facts.text: A manufacturer with no virtual-validation capability must establish all the required specialist domains simultaneously despite scarce skills.
facts.quote: A manufacturer with no capability must stand up all of these domains simultaneously, with scarce skills

facts.text: The booklet favors a hybrid virtual-validation staffing model that buys peak expertise while retaining operating-domain definition, the scenario catalog and correlation data in-house, because a manufacturer starting without capability must establish many domains simultaneously with scarce skills.
facts.quote: which is why the booklet favors a hybrid that buys peak expertise while keeping the operating-domain definition, scenario catalog and correlation data in-house [Chapter 11].
